summary.intent: Investigate and fix the someguy IPNS routing failures that caused staging to revert to delegated-ipfs.dev, then implement a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback with Prometheus metrics, fix the release-please tagging deadlock, and deploy v0.26.2 to staging.
summary.outcome: Someguy was fixed with corrected resource/DHT config, fallback routing with metrics was implemented, the staging tag format was changed from `v*-staging*` to `staging-v*` to stop colliding with release-please's tag discovery, and v0.26.2 was successfully released and deployed to staging (though someguy crashed on staging due to `SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY` expecting raw bytes not a human-readable string).

repo: Someguy v0.11.1 requires SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY as a raw uint64 byte count, not a human-readable string like '1GB'.
The someguy image ships with curl but NOT wget — CodeRabbit's healthcheck warning was correct.
Release-please has never successfully auto-tagged since the major reconfiguration; all prior v* tags were created manually.

Staging pre-release tags in `v{version}-staging-*` format were being scanned by release-please's release discovery (depth: 400) and colliding with root package tag pattern, causing 'Missing 1 paths: .' and the untagged-merged-PRs deadlock.
packages/crypto was missing from release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json, causing it to walk the entire commit history when added.
The release-please Merge plugin produces PR titles like 'chore: release main' — the title pattern mismatch was a red herring; the real issue was staging tag collision.
IPNS resolution is 100% DB-first by design: publishRecord() does fire-and-forget DHT publish while the DB write is synchronous, so DB always wins on sequence number comparison in resolveRecord().
The ThrottlerBypassGuard uses an x-throttle-bypass header with a secret, not NODE_ENV=test — vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env.
The delegated routing client's backend parameter was typed as string instead of 'primary' | 'fallback' union.
Alloy metrics scraping config for someguy had been removed during staging revert and needed restoration.

code.finding: resolveRecord() always queries the DB regardless of network result, then prefers whichever has higher sequence number. Since publishRecord() does fire-and-forget DHT publish after synchronous DB write, DB always has a higher or equal sequence number, making network resolution effectively unused for reads.
backend parameter in recordRequest() metric call was typed as string — should be 'primary' | 'fallback' literal union for type safety.
publishRecord() comment explicitly states 'fire-and-forget — DB is the reliable source of truth', confirming the DB-first architecture is intentional.
vitest does not auto-load .env files — THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET must be passed as an explicit env var on the CLI, not via .env file.
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY must be a raw uint64 byte count (e.g. 1073741824) not a human-readable string like '1GB' — causes crash-loop on start.

workflow: release-please aborts with 'There are untagged, merged release PRs outstanding' when it finds a merged release PR it cannot tag — this is a deadlock that requires manual intervention (create the missing tag + flip label from autorelease:pending to autorelease:tagged).

release-please's release discovery scans up to 400 releases; staging pre-release tags in v* format appear in that scan and can be matched to package paths before the real release, causing 'Missing paths' errors.
Staging tags should use a non-v prefix format (e.g. staging-v0.26.2-rc-1) to avoid colliding with release-please tag discovery.
When adding a new package to release-please without a prior anchor release, it walks the entire commit history — either create an anchor release first or let it do a one-time historical bump.
The release-please GraphQL label mutation can fail with 'Could not resolve node' immediately after PR creation — a transient race condition; manually adding the label fixes it.

Someguy's SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS config does concurrent fanout (race), not sequential fallback — implementing fallback at the API DelegatedRoutingClient layer gives proper fallback semantics and controllable metrics.
Load tests showed someguy has higher median latency (+20-70%) but better tail latency at p99 (-12-22%) vs delegated-ipfs.dev, and zero errors on both — consistent performance is the key advantage.
Vitest throttle bypass: must pass THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET as explicit CLI env var (e.g. THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=xxx pnpm test), not via .env file.

friction: release-please has been broken since the major reconfiguration — every release has required manual tag creation, and the root cause (staging tag collision) took extensive log analysis to find.

Someguy crashed on staging immediately after deploy due to SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY format mismatch — this was not caught locally because the local Docker host may have used a different someguy version or silently ignored the env var.
The ThrottlerBypassGuard uses a header-based secret bypass, not NODE_ENV=test — this was undiscovered until E2E tests all returned 429s, requiring investigation of the guard implementation.
SSH access to the staging VPS was available via a separate root key but not immediately obvious — required prompting from the user.
The staging deploy workflow triggered immediately on tag push without waiting for tag-staging-release to complete, causing an out-of-order deploy.
release-please failed with a transient GraphQL 'Could not resolve node' error when labeling the freshly created PR #327, requiring manual label fix.
The Web E2E check was blocking auto-merge on the release PR — required a re-run and wait cycle.
CodeRabbit's wget vs curl comment was correct but was initially dismissed as 'not applicable' before verification.
open_items: Someguy is crash-looping on staging due to SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY='1GB' — needs fix committed and redeployed (fix was committed at end of session but not yet deployed).
DB-first IPNS resolution means someguy provides zero benefit for read paths — the architectural shift to network-first resolution is deferred until DB load becomes a concern.
packages/crypto has no prior tagged releases and will get a historical version bump (to 0.26.0) on the next release — intentionally deferred.
Mock IPNS routing service remains in docker-compose.yml alongside someguy — intentionally left for CI compatibility, worth revisiting if it causes confusion.
PR #326 (staging tag format fix + crypto release-please config) needs review and merge.

Grafana dashboard panels for the new cipherbox_delegated_routing_requests_total and cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total metrics need to be created — metrics are being emitted but no dashboards or alerts have been configured yet.

The someguy SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS fallback to delegated-ipfs.dev was explicitly NOT configured (fanout vs fallback semantics) — if someguy fallback at the DHT level is desired, this remains unimplemented.
Load test baseline metrics (someguy vs delegated-ipfs.dev JSON files) were saved locally but not committed to the repo.
